Day 35 of 100 · Infrastructure Automation

Jinja2 Templates

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityInfrastructure AutomationPublished after ledger snapshot

Jinja2 templates generate configuration from variables so the structure is reusable while environment-specific values remain data.

Architecture / mental model

template.j2 + variables → Ansible template module → rendered config → service

How it works

The `template` module renders Jinja2 expressions on the control side and writes the resulting file to the managed host with ownership and mode controls.

Templates are strongest when they express configuration, not when they become hidden programs. Keep branching limited and push complicated data shaping into variables or dedicated logic where it is easier to test.

A rendered configuration often needs validation before service reload. That is where the template module's validation support or an explicit check becomes part of safe deployment.

Hands-on reference

ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml
# task uses ansible.builtin.template: src=nginx.conf.j2 dest=/etc/nginx/nginx.conf

Verification

Render into a test path or use the application's native config validator before allowing a handler to reload the service.

Field note / gotcha

A syntactically valid template can render syntactically invalid application configuration. Jinja success is not Nginx/Apache/application validation.

Security considerations

Avoid rendering secrets into world-readable files and set destination ownership/mode explicitly.

What I learned

Templating separates reusable structure from changing values, but the rendered artifact is what the service actually consumes.
